text:
[LNUL.4.2] **Boolean level — Kleene 3-valued logic.** `and` / `or` / `not`
operate over `{true, false, null}` by the standard Kleene tables:

| `a`     | `b`     | `a and b` | `a or b` |
|---------|---------|-----------|----------|
| `true`  | `null`  | `null`    | `true`   |
| `false` | `null`  | `false`   | `null`   |
| `null`  | `null`  | `null`    | `null`   |

and `not true = false`, `not false = true`, `not null = null`.

**A fault is absorbed, not propagated, by a deciding operand.** An operand
faults when evaluating it raises a trap ([LERR.1.4.1]), a `TypeError` or an
`EngineError` ([IRET.9.6]). `and` is `false` if any operand is `false`, wherever
it stands and whatever the others raise; it is a fault only if no operand is
`false`; and it is `null` only if none is `false` and none faults. `or` is the
dual: `true` if any operand is `true`. An implementation may evaluate the
operands in any order and may stop at a deciding operand.

An `EngineError` from anything but evaluating the operand — resource
exhaustion, a `pump_wcet_ns` overrun ([LERR.1.4.7]) — is not an operand's
fault. It halts the tier whatever the expression would answer.

**When several operands fault and none decides,** the expression yields one
fault, chosen by kind first — `EngineError`, then `TypeError`, then the trap
kinds in `proto/engine_error.proto#TrapKind` value order — and within a kind by
the fields of the record the fault is recorded as, in field-number order,
excluding `clock_ns` and `seq` ([RFCS.21.1]): at the first field that differs,
the lower value wins. A string field compares by its UTF-8 bytes as unsigned
values, a proper prefix before any longer string, and a field the record leaves
unset compares as its protobuf default, the empty string or `0`. The
offending operand's slot context ([LERR.9.12]) is among the fields compared.
Two faults that tie on every field record identically. An operand's position never enters, so `a and b` and
`b and a` agree on every input, faults included.

**Absorption and distributivity do not hold once faults exist:** `null and
(null or t)` is the fault `t`, not `null`. Commutativity, associativity, De
Morgan and double negation do.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__best
alloy.note: T2I: the faults no other beats, by kind, then by recorded body. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__ok_where
alloy.note: A well-formed `where`: a trap or TypeError only from a conjunct that can raise by its declared types, null only from a nullable slot; an EngineError from any conjunct -- a value the artefact lied about.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__out
alloy.note: What a conjunct yields: true, false, null, or a fault.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__table
alloy.note: The absorbing `and` folded over the conjuncts: false, then a fault, then null, then true.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__v5_refines_table
alloy.note: V5 REFINES THE TABLE: stopping at the first false in any order and absorbing every fault answers what the table answers. Letting a false not absorb an EngineError breaks it (TEETH).

idris.name: Lnul_4_2__answer
idris.note: The three Kleene values and a fourth, the trap: the clause's domain, which states what and and or do where an operand traps ([LERR.1.4.1]).

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and
idris.note: Kleene and on the three values; A TRAP IS ABSORBED ([LERR.1.4.1]): a false (for or, a true) on either side decides; otherwise a trap on either side is raised; otherwise Kleene's table.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and_commutes
idris.note: and commutes on every input, traps included: the clause's 'a and b and b and a agree on every input'.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__answer_of
idris.note: A result as a truth value: a non-Bool value is an ill-typed where, which the compiler refuses and [IRET.9.6] makes a fault, so it answers as a trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__not
idris.note: Swaps true and false, fixes null; a trap stays a trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__or
idris.note: Kleene or on the three values; A TRAP IS ABSORBED ([LERR.1.4.1]): a false (for or, a true) on either side decides; otherwise a trap on either side is raised; otherwise Kleene's table.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__result_of
idris.note: A truth value as a result again, so a connective's output is an operand.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__table
idris.note: The clause's table, row by row, and its three not cells, by Refl.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__trap_absorbed
idris.note: The cells absorption turns on, as table cells: trap and false, false and trap are false; trap and true traps; the or duals.
